# Random forest regression:
- is a machine learning algorithm used to predict continous
numerical values such as prices, income or temperature
- works by creating many decision tree for anomous prediction

# load built-in dataset
## predict mpg( miles per gallon)
```{r}
data(mtcars)
head(mtcars)
```

- the built-in mtcars


# check structure
```{r}
str(mtcars)
```

# summary statistics
```{r}
describe(mtcars)
```


# check for missing values
```{r}
sum(is.na(mtcars))
colSums(is.na(mtcars))
```

# split data into train and test
```{r}
set.seed(123)
# craetion of train indices
train_index<-createDataPartition(mtcars$mpg, p=.8, list=FALSE)
# training data
train_data<-mtcars[train_index, ]
# testing data
test_data<-mtcars[-train_index,]
```

# check the dimension
```{r}
dim(train_data)
dim(test_data)
```
# Train random forest regression
```{r}
rf_model<- randomForest(
  mpg~.,
  data= train_data,
  ntree=500,
  mtry=3,
  importance= TRUE
)
# view nmodel
print(rf_model)
```


# make predictions using testing set
```{r}
predictions<-predict(rf_model, newdata=test_data)
predictions
```


# evaluate model performance
```{r}
# RMSE
rmse<-RMSE(predictions, test_data$mpg)
# MAE
mae<-MAE(predictions, test_data$mpg)
# R-squared
r2<-R2(predictions, test_data$mpg)
# print results
cat("RMSE",rmse,"\n")
cat("MAE", mae,"\n")
cat("R-squared",r2)
```
# variable importance
```{r}
importance(rf_model)
# plot variable importance
varImpPlot(rf_model)

```


# actual vs predicted plot
```{r}
plot(
  test_data$mpg, 
  predictions,
  main="actual vs predicted",
  xlab=" actual mpg",
  ylab=" predicted mpg",
  pch=19,
  col="skyblue"
)
# add a reghression line
abline(0, 1, col="red", lwd=2)
```

# predict mpg using new data
```{r}
# create a new sample car data
new_car<-data.frame(
  cyl=4,
  disp=120,
  hp=120,
  drat=3.5,
  wt= .8,
  qsec=8,
  vs= 2,
  am=1,
  gear=6,
  carb=3
  
)
# predict mpg
cat("predicted mpg",predict(rf_model, newdata=new_car))
```
```{r}

# 2. Predict mpg for the single new car
single_prediction <- predict(rf_model, newdata = new_car)
cat("Predicted MPG for new car:", single_prediction, "\n")

# 3. Generate predictions on your validation/test set for the scatter plot
# Replace 'test_data' with the actual name of your test dataset variable
test_predictions <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data) 
```



# visualization on new car anhd actual data

# predict mpg using new data
# actual vs predicted plot
```{r}
plot(
  x = test_predictions,          # Predicted values on the X-axis
  y = test_data$mpg,             # Actual values from test data on the Y-axis
  main = "Actual vs. Predicted MPG", 
  xlab = "Predicted MPG", 
  ylab = "Actual MPG", 
  pch = 19, 
  col = "skyblue")
  # Add a 1:1 reference line
abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```
